research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
within-team variation in role coverage across lineups
separability of role coverage from player talent and role counts
talent control in lineup-level influence measures
methodological_questions: Can lineup role coverage be separated from talent and role counts?
Does talent control behave as intended, or does it absorb the role-coverage signal?
What lineup exposure and sample size are needed for stable within-team coverage estimates?
Are the role labels derived from play-by-play measured reliably enough to support the test?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested adaptation quality against talent as predictors of series wins (n=55 series). Talent was significant after control (per-series logistic talent_diff_z +0.737, p=0.0213), while adaptation was not (adapt_diff_z +0.328, p=0.2755). The record states corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124 and that n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality. Failure mechanism recorded as A_unanswerable.

Absence validation: V1(a) gave 16/23 above own-null p95 (binomial p=2.67e-16) and V1(b) gave mean(D_real - median_null)=+0.142, CI [+0.103, +0.187]. V2a Spearman +0.288 (p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667]) and V2b partial +0.253 (p=0.115, CI [-0.262, +0.615]) both failed, with CIs spanning zero.

Structural concentration vs defensive vulnerability (n=117, 30 franchises). C1a rho=+0.079, p=0.0882, CI [-0.114, +0.234]; C1b rho=+0.095, p=0.0738; robust 0.2/0.3 variants also failed. Recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null), though the CI spans 0.

Fragility confirmatory. F1a: structural influence is mostly not reducible to usage (cosine R2=0.094, residual-share=0.906, CI [0.768, 0.962]). F1b: split-half stability of the usage residual, pooled rho=+0.685 (p=0.0000, CI [+0.649, +0.721]), partial rho=+0.557. Recorded as D_positive. Relevant as evidence that residual structural measures can be reproducible, not as a test of lineup coverage.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Separating a structural/adaptation signal from talent as a predictor of outcomes, using talent as a control variable.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded mechanism A_unanswerable: adaptation and talent are correlated (+0.124), the sample is small (n=55 series, 110 directions), and after talent control the adaptation effect is not distinguishable from zero (p=0.275).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of a structural-association change under real player absence (V2a/V2b).
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as FAIL; the confidence intervals span zero and the sample is small (small_sample limitation). The validation step passed (V1), but the magnitude prediction did not.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Hypothesis that concentrated structural influence predicts defensive vulnerability at the franchise level.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as B_powered_null with CI spanning zero and a low-power, large-MDE limitation (30 franchises, n=117). This is a null result, not a method fault, but it shows the team-level sample is thin.

evidence_establishes: Earlier projects in this series, using comparable per-game and derived structural data, found that talent-controlled structural or adaptation effects were not separable at small team- or series-level n (FAM:SF-APPS-027, FAM:SF-PAP-024).
Structural-influence residuals can be reproducible across split halves once usage is partialled out (FAM:SF18), which supports measuring structural measures but not the lineup-coverage question.
Talent and structural/adaptation measures have been shown to be correlated enough to threaten separability (FAM:SF-APPS-027: corr=+0.124).
Small team- or series-level samples have repeatedly produced unresolved or null results on talent-controlled structural questions.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests lineup coverage of organizer, shaper or terminal roles. None of the four records defines these roles, measures within-team lineup coverage, or tests its separability from talent and counts.
No record establishes whether the NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 play-by-play data yields reliable role labels at the lineup level.
No record gives the power of a lineup-level design with 420,993 possessions. The records are at series, franchise, or absence-event level, so their power figures do not transfer.
No record shows that talent control, as currently specified, behaves correctly for lineup-level coverage.
Whether the 2025-26 partial data would be a valid confirmatory sample is not addressed by any record.
own_inferences: The question as posed bundles three claims: that coverage varies within team, that it is separable from talent and counts, and that talent control behaves. Only the first is directly observable. The other two depend on operational definitions the task does not supply.

Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper or terminal) is probably mechanically tied to role counts and to player quality, because better and more numerous players are more likely to supply each role. Separation therefore requires a design where the coverage indicator varies while counts and talent are held fixed, which the data may not support.
Talent measured from the same season as the outcome creates leakage. A prior-season or leave-out talent measure is needed.
Within-team variation may be too small to estimate reliably at the lineup level unless minutes are pooled across many lineups per team-season.
The records' status labels (untestable, rejected, supported) are automated labels. This review cites them as recorded and does not re-derive them.
uncertainties: The operational definitions of organizer, shaper and terminal are not in the task statement. The glossary and data catalog were not consulted, so the derived play-type field mappings are unverified.
The number of lineups per team-season with adequate possessions is unknown.
How the derived play-type possession records were built from play-by-play (initiator, play type, points) is not documented here; possible label errors are unknown.
Whether 2025-26 regular-season data (complete from 2026-04-13) and playoff data (complete from 2026-06-21) can be used without leakage depends on the as-of date, which is 2026-07-13.
Retrieval returned four family records, all on adjacent questions. Further retrieval might surface a closer family, but none was returned.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records are adjacent, not direct, but they consistently show that talent-controlled structural effects are not separable at small n and that talent control is a live confounder. Together with the absence of any role-coverage record, this moved the decision from a provisional proceed to do_not_proceed as posed. A restricted, pre-registered design is still given below as the minimum viable test.

blocking_constraints.text: Lineup role coverage is likely correlated with talent and role counts. Without a talent measure that is not contaminated by the outcome, separability cannot be claimed.

Organizer, shaper and terminal labels are derived from play-by-play possession records (initiator, play type, points). If the labels use the outcome, the coverage-outcome association is partly circular.
Role labels are not validated. Their reliability at the lineup level is unknown.
90 team-seasons is a small base for within-team lineup contrasts, and the prior records show that small team- and series-level samples yielded untestable or null results.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record addresses lineup coverage of organizer, shaper or terminal roles. The adjacent records cover adaptation vs talent (untestable), absence validation (untestable), structural concentration vs defensive vulnerability (rejected as a powered null) and fragility of residual influence (supported). They inform the talent-confounding and small-sample risks but do not answer the question.

risks.text: Talent and role counts are likely correlated with coverage. The prior SF-APPS-027 record found talent and adaptation correlated (+0.124), and talent absorbed the effect.
90 team-seasons and within-team lineup strata may give too few lineups per cell. SF-APPS-027 (n=55) and SF-PAP-024 (30 franchises) were both underpowered or unresolved.
Roles derived from initiator and points fields may encode the same outcome being predicted.
Lineups with the three roles present may have few possessions, leaving unstable coverage estimates.
Role labels have no recorded reliability; a split-half check is needed. SF18 showed reproducibility for a different measure only.
Talent measured in-season, or using partial 2025-26 data before the completion dates, would leak outcome information.
SF20 shows that a validation can pass while the magnitude prediction fails. A placebo design must be pre-specified to avoid reading a single passing check as support.
Three roles, several coverage thresholds and several talent specifications multiply the comparisons.
Roster and role patterns change across the four seasons, and 2025-26 is partly complete.
Play-type mapping and the initiator assignment from play-by-play may be misclassified, and the error rate is unknown.

design.estimand: Within-team association between lineup coverage of at least one organizer, shaper or terminal (indicator, and count) and possession-level points per possession, conditional on prior-season player talent and role counts. Separation is tested as: the residual variance of coverage after regressing on talent and counts is above a pre-set threshold.
design.unit: Lineup-season (five-player unit within team-season) with a pre-set minimum possession count; possession is the outcome observation.
design.sample: Development: 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons. Confirmatory: 2025-26 regular season, used only after its completion on 2026-04-13. Playoffs excluded from confirmation. The 2025-26 playoff data is excluded until complete (from 2026-06-21).
design.power: Simulation-based power analysis before analysis, using observed lineup possession distributions. Target power of at least 0.8 for the pre-specified effect size on the coverage coefficient. If power is inadequate, report the test as untestable rather than null.
design.controls: Talent from prior-season player ratings only (no in-season or same-season information). Role counts. Minutes, pace, opponent strength, team fixed effects. Clustered standard errors by team-season.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo role labels, shuffled within team-season while matching counts, must show no association. (2) A non-possession outcome (for example, pre-game or non-shot events) must show no association. (3) A talent-only model must be compared with the coverage model to check the talent control behaves as intended.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-specified primary coefficient (any-role coverage indicator). Secondary role-specific and threshold analyses corrected by Holm.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to confirmatory test only if: role-label split-half reliability is above a pre-specified threshold; the separability residual variance is above threshold; power is adequate. Support requires the primary coefficient to clear the pre-set CI and the placebo checks to be null. Otherwise report untestable or uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters and derived play-type possession records for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons, using only data complete as of 2026-07-13 (2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs excluded until complete).

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
